question: linux-x1 gated the cleanup on ARM GNU 14.2.1 and windows-desk on ARM GNU 14.3.1. This is the same gate on xPack 15.2.1, which is the project's third install and second code generator, and the one #54 showed the whole codegen axis rests on.
after_note: 63c92f3 is 766c951 plus three DOC-ONLY commits - verified with git diff --stat 766c951 63c92f3 over drivers, lib, apps, sketches, bsp, linker, cmake and CMakeLists.txt, which is empty. The image under test is 766c951's firmware.
cc: GCC: (xPack GNU Arm Embedded GCC x86_64) 15.2.1 20251203
instrument: tools/image_mnemonics.py at 766c951 - the FIXED tool - copied out of the tree first and run against both ELFs of every pair. Each revision's own copy would have compared a buggy hash against a fixed one.
method: Both revisions built IN PLACE in the main checkout under the same build directory names, so the build path is byte-identical across each pair. A worktree was tried first and could not configure: the xPack toolchain lives at tools/xpack-* inside the main checkout and is gitignored, so a worktree cannot see it, and -DARM_TOOLCHAIN_DIR does not propagate into CMake's try_compile sub-project. In-place checkout removes the path variable linux-x1 retracted over, rather than working around it.
track_c_note: build-c was configured on this bench for the first time for this run - FreeRTOS V11.1.0, f388a5c8078e152913e4eb3c5d75bf89561392df. This bench can gate Track C from now on.

positive_control.what: one __asm__ volatile("nop") as the first statement of main() in apps/baremetal_bringup/main.c, Track B, same path and same tool, then reverted with git checkout and rebuilt
positive_control.why: a hash that cannot detect a change produces an all-identical table for the wrong reason. windows-desk ran this control on 14.3.1; a control run on another bench certifies that bench's instrument, not this one's.
positive_control.means: the hash discriminates on this compiler too, and the revert restores it exactly. The INSTRUCTION COUNT DID NOT MOVE - 10,345 either way.
positive_control.the_catch: Independent reproduction of windows-desk's finding on a different code generator: the injected nop consumes alignment padding, so a count-based gate passes a real code change. Two compilers now agree that n_instructions is the weaker instrument. Quote the hash.

behaviour.flashed: manually with tools/flash.py before run 1, logged at 63c92f3, cc and layout populated. This sidesteps the trap windows-desk named: the suite flashes only when the board's TRACK disagrees with --track, so a new image of a track the board already runs is silently not flashed.

discarded_run.note: first suite after a flash. Reported, not relied on - CLAUDE.md's rule is to drop run 1 by index, not by a filter on what run 1 is thought to do wrong.

behaviour.delta_between_runs: one test moved column: test_device_receives_every_byte_the_host_sent[b-28] passed in run 1 and xfailed in run 2, losing 384 B = 3 x 128-byte chunks. RC 28 is in the test's own RESIDUAL = {32, 28} set and 128-byte chunks are the documented macOS under-pressure shape, so this is a known intermittent category, not a new defect. It is also why run 1 is discarded rather than averaged.
behaviour.vs_other_benches: 590/9/4 here against linux-x1's 585/16/2 and windows-desk's 586/16/1. The pass difference is fewer skips, not more tests: this bench has a host GNU compiler at /usr/bin so test_framer_close builds and runs, which windows-desk skips. The extra xfails are macOS's own byte loss at RC 44 and RC 39 (OVERSUPPLIED), which neither Windows nor Linux hits. test_host_fed_ramp_loses_no_samples[b], the alternating #24 xfail, landed on the pass side in both runs here.

dso_gap: test_scope.py skips 4 cases here too - 'no known scope found; looked for 1ab1:0588'. This desk lost its DS1102E and DAC1 moved to A1 on 2026-09-01, so tools/dso_metrics.py is now unexercised on ALL THREE benches. The gap linux-x1 and windows-desk each reported as theirs is project-wide and nobody should be waiting on this bench to close it.
not_claimed: that these hashes should match the other benches' - xPack 15.2.1 is a different code generator and 10,345 against windows-desk's 10,342 and linux-x1's 10,510 on Track B is expected
that Track A or Track C BEHAVE correctly here - only their images were gated; neither suite was run
that the RC 28 residual in run 2 is new - it is inside the test's documented RESIDUAL set
that a scope gap can be closed here - the instrument is gone from this desk, not merely idle
